heading: **27 October 2025**
body:
### 1. MNase digestion & testing of new reconstituted samples

Take 50 ng of each sample:

i. 293T-20K (   uL) \+ 5 uL Buffer \+ 0.25 uL rAlbumin \+ 1 uL dil-MNase

ii. GP5d-20K (   uL) \+ 5 uL Buffer \+ 0.25 uL rAlbumin \+ 1 uL dil-MNase

iii. D4recon ( uL) \+ 5 uL Buffer \+ 0.25 uL rAlbumin \+ 1 uL dil-MNase

iv. D5recon ( uL) \+ 5 uL Buffer \+ 0.25 uL rAlbumin \+ 1 uL dil-MNase

v. D6recon ( uL) \+ 5 uL Buffer \+ 0.25 uL rAlbumin \+ 1 uL dil-MNase

Incubate at 37 degrees, 2 mins. Add 1.1 uL EGTA (0.5 M) to stop the reaction. Run these samples on a 0.5 % agarose gel and stain with SYBR Green.

Stain the gel with SYBR green.

### 2. *Hia5* treatment for D4, D5 and D6 recon problems

D4 and D5-1 samples contained some level of the refolding buffer by mistake during the post salt exchange dialysis clean-up.

If these samples showed good results in the MNase assay, then this extra salt has not created significant issues.

*Estimating the salt levels*

D4recon \~ 100 uL volume with \~20 uL refolding buffer ⇒ I estimate the salt concentration to be \~450 mM at this point in the mix

For D4 based on the concentration I estimate using about 200 ng DNA per Hia5 reaction, this would be 7.2 uL per reaction. After making up this reaction completely, the salt concentration would be \~200 mM.

I am just going to dialyse D4 and D5-1 again 2-3 times with 15 mL each of nucleosome buffer C to ensure that the salt level goes back down to 80 mM before Hia5 treatment.

### 3. lig147 ligand plate preparation

Based on lig147 PCR2, the concentration of the samples was 19.9 ng/uL.

Volume of lig147 needed for one plate ⇒ 400 X 15 \= 6000 uL

Total amount of DNA \= 6000 x 25 \= 150 ug

Concentration of original lig147 ssDNA tube is about 4.8 ug/uL

Dilute this 1:200 ⇒ 1 uL oligo \+ 199 uL TE buffer (lig147-dil200)

PCR 1 → 100X
